title: Graduated-fallback orchestrator with cohort-regression sentinel
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build a policy engine that drives graduated traffic shifts for model rollouts while continuously evaluating cohort-level regressions and enabling fast, deterministic fallback when quality or cost SLOs break. This ticket covers the configuration DSL, local simulator hooks, telemetry contracts, and the orchestrator that executes step schedules and fallback actions.

Problem statement: Current rollout tooling can split traffic and progress steps, but lacks: 1) cohort-aware regression detection (small regressions in a subpopulation often missed by global aggregates), 2) graduated fallback that can attenuate traffic by cohort instead of global rollback, and 3) a compact, expressive configuration that pairs step schedules with multi-criteria guardrails (latency, perplexity/regression deltas, token cost, error rate).

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement UI for manual override (Console work will follow) and does not add new metric ingesters — it assumes existing telemetry pipeline exposes per-cohort metrics and drift signals.

Design proposal:
- Configuration DSL: JSON/YAML schema that declares: cohorts (by header/segment rules), steps (time or traffic-based), conditional gates (metric, delta window, threshold), attenuation policies (percent step-down, cohort-only cut), and recovery behaviors (automatic re-progression after stability window). Provide example: {"cohorts": [{"name":"mobile_v1","rule":"user_agent:mobile"}], "steps": [{"name":"step1","at":"10%","duration":"6h"}], "guards": [{"metric":"latency_p95","operator":">","threshold":"200ms","action":"attenuate:50%","scope":"cohort"}] }.
- Cohort-regression sentinel: streaming comparator that computes per-cohort deltas against baseline model for configured test metrics (latency_p95, failure_rate, expected_quality_score). Uses rolling windows (5m, 1h) and an outlier detection layer (bootstrap CI) to avoid noisy single-window flips.
- Graduated fallback actions: when guard triggers, orchestrator applies smallest scoped action first (attenuate within cohort), then escalate to route-wide attenuation, and finally hard rollback to previous model if escalation thresholds are met. All actions are idempotent and recorded in the rollout trace.
- Simulator & safety checks: a local simulator that can execute DSL plans against historical request logs and synthetic cohorts, producing estimated cost and failure scenarios. Simulator must run in CI and flag plans that could cause >10% request interruption or immediate SLA violations.
- Telemetry & observability: rollout traces include step-by-step traffic percentages, guard evaluations, trigger timestamps, and action execution IDs. Add telemetry tags for cohort, step, guard_id, and evidence (metric snapshots). Console will visualize but runtime must export structured events to our tracing backend and incremental metrics to metrics pipeline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement DSL parser and validation with unit tests and examples.
- Implement orchestrator state machine able to: start rollout, progress steps on schedule, evaluate guards, apply attenuation/rollback actions, and recover after stability.
- Implement cohort-regression sentinel library and wire it to the guard evaluator using an abstraction over metrics sources.
- Add simulator harness and CI gating test that runs a plan against a sampled request log and reports safety violations.
- End-to-end integration test: run a synthetic rollout in staging that triggers an attenuation on a cohort and verify orchestrator executes the correct escalation sequence and records telemetry.

Risks & mitigations:
- Metric noise causing false positives: mitigate with multi-window checks + minimum event counts + bootstrap CIs.
- Partial enforcement across dedicated/private deployments: provide a config feature-flag and fallback to conservative defaults if cohort telemetry is missing.
- Complexity of DSL misuse: include strict schema validation, ergonomic CLI plan linter, and simulator checks before plan acceptance.

Next steps / implementation tasks (high level):
1) Schema & parser: define DSL (2d design + 3d implementation).
2) Cohort sentinel: library + unit tests (5d).
3) Orchestrator state machine & action executor (6d).
4) Simulator and CI integration (4d).
5) Staging runbook and integration tests (3d).
